feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications/platform leader with clear domain focus and solid progression at NACo. It shows breadth and technical depth well, but it is somewhat dense, repetitive across sections, and could sharpen impact by emphasizing outcomes over responsibilities.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear positioning: the headline, summary, and experience consistently support a senior digital/platform leadership profile in public-sector communications.  
- Strong credibility: long tenure and progression within one organization, plus concrete scale indicators like “10,000+ page website” and “3.5 million annual page views.”  
- Good skills coverage: combines strategy, governance, analytics, CMS, multimedia, and AI/search in a way that feels current and relevant.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve structure and scannability.  
- Add more measurable outcomes: several bullets describe duties (“advise,” “develop,” “strengthened”) without showing results such as engagement gains, efficiency improvements, or adoption.  
- Fix style consistency and minor writing issues: use consistent punctuation in lists, avoid mixed list formatting in paragraph bullets, and standardize terms like “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s.” No major misspellings found; grammar is generally strong. Minor stylistic inconsistency: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear seniority and domain focus. It reads well, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten the first sentence and foreground scale/outcomes: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years shaping platforms, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with stronger, more executive phrasing such as “shaping” or “leading” to better match director-level experience.
- Streamline the second sentence to group capabilities more cleanly: “Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- Consider adding one concrete scale marker from recent roles if space allows, e.g., “10,000+ page websites” or “3.5M annual page views.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; keep it brief here.
- “Platforms, governance models and content operations” closely echoes multiple skills sections, so avoid adding more capability lists in the intro.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong and relevant, but it overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership themes will make it feel more distinctive and less repetitive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider a sharper, less repetitive version: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting and optimization • Cross-channel communications leadership • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia and livestream production
- Replace “content experiences” with “content discovery” to sound more specific and aligned with the AI search project.
- Change “Multi-channel communications operations” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Use “and” instead of “&” for consistency with the rest of the CV’s more formal style.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section substantially repeats the header summary and Topline Skills; consider shortening to 6 items or using it only for themes not already named elsewhere.
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with Topline Skills: “Public-sector and advocacy messaging.”
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Convert to a cleaner list format with parallel verbs and tighter phrasing; e.g., “Created AI-enabled legislative search using hybrid retrieval, vector search, structured content workflows, and bill-level chat.”
- Prioritize the most recent/highest-value projects first and consider adding 1 concrete result, audience, or scale metric where available.
- Standardize style: use consistent punctuation, avoid “Designed/Built/Developed” repetition, and spell out “10 x 20-foot” consistently.
- Clarify campaign names if possible; “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is vague compared with the other titles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series substantially overlap with current NACo consulting and prior NACo role bullets.
- “Editorial storytelling,” “modular structure,” and “distribution across website, email and social” echo language already used elsewhere in the CV.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the NACo role below and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level impact, platform modernization, and the AI search initiative.

Suggested edit
- Recast into 3 impact-led bullets; start with outcomes/themes, not “Consult.”
- Add scale/results where possible: number of sites/pages, stakeholders, campaign launches, workflow time saved, search/discovery improvements, engagement gains.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, web governance, and content operations, strengthening cross-channel communications across web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Built Drupal-based campaign and storytelling experiences—including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member toolkits—while providing front-end implementation and support for public-facing web properties.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content workflows, and discovery UX to improve access to complex policy and member content.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics” overlaps with the prior Director role unless you specify what is new in this consulting engagement.
- Microsite/campaign examples duplicate Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level and let the project section carry specifics.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management points already covered in adjacent NACo roles.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/outcome line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web modernization, analytics, governance, multimedia operations, and budget oversight across website, email, social, and video.”
- Make bullets more results-led: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Strengthen impact language where metrics are missing: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, reducing reliance on external production and expanding capacity for advocacy, events, and recurring multimedia content.”
- Combine/trim channel oversight + governance bullets; add team size, budget, engagement growth, reporting efficiency, or publishing-speed improvements if available.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Governance/editorial systems also appear in the summary and consultant role; use one concise bullet here, not multiple.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but the item reads generic and overlaps with both the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager/Producer role. Tighten it around operational leadership, editorial systems, and channel growth at this career stage.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the opening with: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets to emphasize ownership and outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet for impact: “Produced and grew a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets: “Improved editorial planning, cross-team coordination and digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helping scale” and “helped improve” weaken impact; use direct action verbs.
- Avoid repeating website/email/social/video platform leadership already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, core competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than repeating generic communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less generic phrasing:
- Enterprise digital strategy & modernization
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Content operations leadership” if you want stronger alignment with your recent systems/governance work.
- If space allows elsewhere, add one proof point near this section header, e.g. “10,000+ page Drupal migration” or “3.5M annual page views,” since skills alone read abstract.
- Keep terms consistent with recent experience: use “governance,” “operations,” and “modernization,” which are stronger than “messaging.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and recent execution rather than exhaustive technologies.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters tied to recent work: “Drupal platform leadership • CMS modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search and discovery”
- Drop lower-signal or older/admin tools here unless central to target roles; keep WordPress, SharePoint, and Power Pages only if job-relevant.
- Replace “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” with “Front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript)” for concision; jQuery can live in Technical + IT.
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “Drupal platform leadership for 10,000+ page, 3.5M annual page-view environment.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates the detailed stack already listed under “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills more strategic.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies, header, and projects—mention once here at most.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for the recent director/consulting work, but it reads as a tool dump and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” Make it more outcome-oriented and leadership-level.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-only to capability + tools: “Analytics strategy, KPI design and executive reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity • SEO, UX and performance analysis”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing: “Executive dashboards and decision support” or “Executive reporting and performance insights”
- Add one optimization concept if accurate: “Measurement frameworks,” “Conversion analysis,” or “Experimentation/A/B testing”
- Keep to 3–5 grouped phrases rather than 8 separate items for cleaner scanability

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Core Competencies: Analytics and reporting infrastructure” and “Technical + IT: Data, Analytics & Optimization”; use this section for higher-level capabilities, not another software list.
- “SEO and performance analysis” overlaps with Technical + IT; consider keeping the tools there and the strategic framing here.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill cluster, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Core Competencies” and multiple NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and tools that support leadership-level multimedia delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from task list to capability set: “Broadcast-quality video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • In-house studio operations • PTZ camera systems and multi-camera workflows”
- Replace “Video production and editing” with a more senior phrase like “Broadcast-quality video production” or “End-to-end video production” to better match the studio build and advocacy programming work.
- Consider adding one specificity cue from the CV’s recent experience, e.g. “advocacy programming” or “recurring multimedia content,” if style allows.
- Keep to 4 items max and order by strategic value: livestream/hybrid events, studio operations, video production, PTZ/multi-camera systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “multimedia production” duplicate the Core Competencies line “Multimedia production and livestream operations.”
- “Hybrid and virtual event production” overlaps with “event production” already implied in the Director of Digital Media entry.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. This item should either add specificity on level of use or be trimmed to emphasize the most current, highest-value platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers to show depth without turning this into a full skills paragraph: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites, governance) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, sharpen for seniority: **Enterprise CMS: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Consider dropping **GitHub Pages** if it was only occasional use; it reads less strategic than the others.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep one version broader and this one more tool-specific.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so avoid overexplaining it here.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical breadth, but this reads like a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools you actively use in recent work and group items more strategically.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second grouped phrase: “Technical integrations: APIs, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- Consider replacing older/basic terms with stronger, current framing if accurate: e.g., “custom front-end development” instead of listing HTML5/CSS3 separately.
- If possible, connect to impact elsewhere in the CV by reflecting recent use cases: GTM for analytics deployment, Workers for lightweight web apps/search tooling, GitHub Actions for deployment automation.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization unless you specifically want to stress implementation.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since automation is already emphasized elsewhere, this item should be tighter and framed around systems you actively build or manage.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/impact: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Trello • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers instead of a bare list: **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp (project workflows) • Slack/Teams (cross-team coordination)**
- Consider dropping 1–2 lower-value tools if space is tight; emphasize platforms tied to enterprise workflow design, not basic collaboration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies and Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; listing both can dilute seniority unless positioned as collaboration systems within broader workflow operations.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Relevant tools, but this item is too bare and misses a chance to signal scale and current-platform relevance. It should align more clearly with the recent NACo email/newsletter work without repeating role bullets.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely depth/relevance: **Higher Logic • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional context instead of just names: **Higher Logic (member email/newsletters) • Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (journey orchestration/segmentation) • Mailchimp (campaign delivery)**
- If one platform was primary in recent roles, consider a qualifier: **Higher Logic (primary)** to emphasize recency.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding outcomes like “tens of thousands of recipients” here; that’s already covered well in Work Experience.
- Don’t repeat generic “multi-channel communications” language already captured in Core Competencies and role descriptions.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills” and recent NACo experience. Tighten it to emphasize methods and business use, not just repeat platform names.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics, Experimentation & Reporting**
- Rewrite as: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • KPI design • Dashboard reporting • SEO analysis • A/B testing**
- Put the highest-value, most strategic items first: analytics stack, then reporting/measurement methods, then optimization tactics.
- If you have proof points, align wording to outcomes already implied elsewhere, e.g., “executive dashboarding,” “performance analysis,” or “conversion optimization” rather than generic “Dashboarding.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates **Topline Skills [3] Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider merging or making one tools-only and the other outcomes-focused.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating the exact same phrasing.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal and good scope for an earlier role, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo entries on workflows, video, and digital operations. Make it more execution-focused and anchor it in “firsts” or scale.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize progression and concrete contributions: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping launch NACo’s first in-house digital team.”
- Tighten scope into 2–3 impact areas: website refresh, recurring multimedia production, and junior staff support.
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of livestreams/events produced, cadence of weekly videos, audience growth, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles and helped launch NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates for member communications, and improved day-to-day workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Provided direct guidance to a digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” overlaps with the 2018–2024 roles; use more tactical wording here.
- “Weekly video updates” is close to the later advocacy video bullet; distinguish this as an earlier build-out phase.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, scripting, production, and rollout.”
- Replace “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more active, specific phrase like “produced digital and multimedia content for program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable result: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported member engagement.
- Keep this entry brief since later roles show broader digital leadership; position it as the starting point of your multimedia/digital progression.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later video/media roles; keep this item focused on podcast launch and innovation/project coordination.
- Avoid repeating broad digital operations language already covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful skills, but this item reads as a mixed list of software and capabilities, and it overlaps heavily with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize tools here and leave broader production strengths to higher-level sections.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Creative Software & Production Tools**
- Rewrite as: **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Podcast recording/editing • Livestream production workflows**
